summary: Aleksandra Turek is an Indologist who studied at the University of Warsaw from 1996 to 2009, earning her M.A. and Ph.D. In 2010, she became an assistant professor there.

Aleksei Davydovich Litman (1923–1992) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at Moscow State University around 1945–1950. He served as Secretary at the Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Tajikistan (1951–1956) and joined the Institute of Oriental Studies in 1957.

Aleksei Dyakov (1896–1974) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Moscow State University (1913–1914, ~1916–1921) and Tomsk State University (1914–1919), later serving as a professor at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1950.

Aleksei Osipovich Ivanovskii (1863–1903) was a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1881 and under Vasily Vasiliev, Aleksey Pozdneev, and Ivan Pavlovich Minaev (~1881–1885), succeeding Sergey Georgiyevsky in 1894.

Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov (1890–1952) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv under Friedrich Knauer, Sergey Oldenburg, and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. He taught at Saint Petersburg State University and directed the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Aleksej Stepanovič Barhudarov (1927–2001) worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg State University (~1945–1950). He served at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1953–1971) and joined the Institute of Linguistics in 1971.

Aleksey Sergeevich Sukhochev (1928–2000) was an Indologist who studied at Moscow State University around 1952–1957. In 1956, he became a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
Aleksey Shakhmatov studied under Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov and Theodor Korsch between approximately 1883 and 1887.

Alessandro Giudice is an Indologist who earned an MA at the University of Pisa (2020–2022) and undertook PhD studies at the University of Cagliari (2022–2026). His posts include cultore della materia at Pisa (2023) and Cagliari (2025).

Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. He has held positions as a university assistant at the University of Vienna (attested 2022), principal investigator at IKGA (attested 2022), and part-time assistant professor at the University of Toronto (attested 2026).
Alessandro Veniero was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Catania in 1917 and as principal at Liceo di Macerata from 1918 to 1919.

Alex McKay (born 1953) is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1995. He has held fellowships at SOAS, the International Institute for Asian Studies, and University College London.

Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Oxford (BA) and SOAS (MA), and was supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include positions at Wolfson College, Oxford, Harvard University, and Ashoka University.

Alex Wayman (1921–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at UCLA and UC Berkeley under Ferdinand Lessing and Murray Barnson Emeneau, he held posts at Wisconsin–Madison, Columbia University, and UC Berkeley.

Alexander B. Nicholson (1848–1906) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After graduating from Princeton Theological Seminary in 1864, he served at Queen's University of Ireland from 1878, becoming Professor of Comparative Philology and Sanskrit in 1902.

Alexander Berzin (born 1944) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard (PhD, under Masatoshi Nagatomi) and co-founded the Translation Bureau at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1972–1998).

Alexander Coburn Soper (1904–1993) worked in archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned degrees from Hamilton College and Princeton University (PhD 1944), later serving as professor at Bryn Mawr College and New York University, and editor of Artibus Asiae.

Alexander Cunningham (1814–1893) worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at Addiscombe Military Seminary and under James Prinsep. He founded the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as its Archaeological Surveyor (1861–1865) and Director-General (1871–1885).

Alexander Duff (1806–1878) worked in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and the University of St Andrews (~1821–1829), and taught Krishna Mohan Banerjee.

Alexander Duncan Campbell (1786–1857) worked in linguistics and Indology. In 1816, he served on the Board of Superintendence at the College of Fort St. George, and he was active in the Madras Literary Society from around 1818 to 1842.
